commits.edited_message:
parsedate: time zone strings

The single and two letter names are not used for lookup anymore so drop
them. The three and four letter versions are now stored as uint32 to
use less memory and get found slightly faster.

Filter on the first letter once up front instead of once per length
branch: every zone name starts with an uppercase letter.

Closes #23000

parsedate: remove the unused leading three letters

The three first letters of the weekdays are never actually used in the
weekday array so drop them. Also make the array local.

Also drop the first letter range checks in checktz: unknown names are
rejected by the lookups themselves, two-letter names are only accepted
for NT and UT and the others have to be found in the sorted tables.
Keep the shared filter for non-letters.

Closes #23013

coupling:
Defect: OOB read of the static 26-entry (52-byte) table tzone[] in checktz() (lib/parsedate.c). The len==1 fast path returns tzone[first - 'A'] with no upper bound on `first`, so any single lowercase letter token (e.g. 'm', index 43 -> byte offset 86, 36 bytes past the 52-byte global) reads out of bounds. Reached from the public API curl_getdate(), whose documented contract is to return -1 for anything unparseable - libcurl itself feeds it attacker-influenced Date/Expires/Last-Modified header content, and datestring() routes any alpha token that is not a weekday/month name to checktz().

How it is split across the two commits:
- Edit of 791f5e19d7 ('parsedate: time zone strings'): this commit reworks checktz and centrally filters the first letter. The edit is a pure dedup refactor: it hoists the existing inline (first > 'Z') bound from the len==1 branch into the shared first-letter guard (now (first < 'A') || (first > 'Z')) and reduces the len==1 branch to if(first == 'J'). Behavior-identical on every input; on its own this tree is safe because the hoisted guard still rejects lowercase before the table index.
- Edit of a3e2e44cbe ('parsedate: remove the unused leading three letters'): this commit's real change is to the weekday array; the edit additionally removes first-letter range checks, arguing that the lookups reject unknown names on their own. That argument is true for len==2 (only NT/UT accepted), len==3/4 (bsearch miss) - which is why the removed (first > 'Y')/(first > 'W') prefilters really were redundant - but silently false for len==1, whose tzone[first - 'A'] direct index has no lookup of its own; its only upper bound was the guard the first commit had centralized and this edit drops.

Why the fix is non-local: the bug is reachable only when commit 1's hoisted guard loses its upper bound via commit 2. Verified empirically: the original batch, the batch with only the 791f5e19d7 edit applied, and the batch with only the a3e2e44cbe edit applied (which keeps the original inline (first > 'Z') in len==1) all run the PoC clean under ASan (rc=0, no report); only the composition aborts (rc=134, global-buffer-overflow READ of size 2 in checktz). Reverting either single edit restores a bound that covers the len==1 index - on the 791f5e19d7 side by restoring the inline check, on the a3e2e44cbe side because the original len==1 branch still carries (first > 'Z') - so a correct fix must reconcile the guard across both commits, e.g. keep the upper bound in whichever single place guards the tzone[] index.
